# CANDIDATE: HARD_ENTRY_CUTOFF_1500

**Filed:** 2026-07-12  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

ENTER signals emitted after 15:00 ET often result in poor fills and increased losses due to thinning liquidity and the imminent 15:50 ET time stop. These "ghost entries" disproportionately affect losing days by adding avoidable losses. Implementing a hard entry cutoff at 15:00 ET will reduce late-day losing trades without impacting early-day winner trades, improving edge capture on losing days.

## Mechanism

Modify the entry gate in `entry_gate_timing.py` to reject any ENTER signal when the current time is 15:00 ET or later. The exit logic (chart stop, profit-lock chandelier, existing 15:50 ET time stop) remains unchanged. Entries before 15:00 ET proceed as normal, subject to all other filters and triggers.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper account ~= 14% headline P&L scaling.
2. **Sample bias:** Proposal based on anecdotal observation of late-day losses; no historical sample analyzed yet. High overfit risk if implemented without validation.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (requires walk-forward held-out window test).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (requires real OPRA fill simulation on top 3 J days).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst case: cuts off valid late-day entries on strong trend days (e.g., 5/04 runner extension), turning winners into smaller profits or losers. Max drawdown could increase if winners are truncated. Blow-up scenario: multiple stopped-out trades near cutoff cause whipsaw losses.
6. **Concentration:** Unknown -- requires backtest. If top-5 days currently contribute X% of P&L, this change may alter concentration by reducing late-day losers.

## Pre-merge gate

Must pass: gym validators (entry_gate_timing.py unit tests), walk-forward OOS test (Sharpe > 0.5), real-fills validation on top 3 J days (diff < ±20% vs BS sim), and OP-16 anchor regression test (no winner regression, loss reduction on losers).

## Confidence

6 / 10 -- Rationale: Intuitive liquidity/time-decay argument, but requires empirical validation to confirm net edge impact. Late-day entries may contain hidden winners that offset loser reduction.
